symmetries: Antisymmetric: F_{μν} = -F_{νμ}, so the diagonal vanishes — F_{μμ} = 0
6 independent components in 4D spacetime: 3 electric (E_x, E_y, E_z) and 3 magnetic (B_x, B_y, B_z)
F is a closed differential 2-form: dF = 0 (when F = dA), which encodes the homogeneous Maxwell equations
Under Lorentz boosts (velocity β along x): E_y → γ(E_y - βcB_z), B_z → γ(B_z - βE_y/c) — E and B mix
invariants: FIRST INVARIANT — Lorentz scalar: I₁ = F_{μν}F^{μν} = 2(B² - E²/c²)
since F^{0i} = η^{00}η^{ii}F_{0i} = (+1)(-1)(E_i/c) = -E_i/c contributes negative sign
Classification: I₁ > 0 → magnetic-type field (B² > E²/c²); I₁ < 0 → electric-type; I₁ = 0 → null or mixed
SECOND INVARIANT — Lorentz pseudoscalar: I₂ = F_{μν}*F^{μν} = (1/2)ε^{μνρσ}F_{μν}F_{ρσ} = -4(E⃗·B⃗)/c
where *F^{μν} = (1/2)ε^{μνρσ}F_{ρσ} is the Hodge dual (ε^{0123} = -1 for signature +−−−)
The dual swaps roles: *F_{0i} = B_i, *F_{ij} = ε_{ijk}E_k/c
Pseudoscalar: changes sign under parity (P) or time reversal (T); invariant under proper orthochronous Lorentz group
Classification: I₂ = 0 → E⃗ ⊥ B⃗ in every frame; I₂ ≠ 0 → E·B is an absolute fact, no boost removes it
COMPLETENESS: By Cayley-Hamilton applied to the linear map F^μ_ν, these two are the only algebraically independent invariants for a rank-2 antisymmetric tensor in 4D
tensorProperties.indexStructure: (0,2) antisymmetric tensor — element of the exterior algebra Λ²(T*M)
tensorProperties.coordinateSystem: Minkowski, signature (+,−,−,−), coordinates x^μ = (ct, x, y, z)

physicalInterpretation.units: F_{0i}: V·m⁻¹ = kg·m·A⁻¹·s⁻³ (electric field / c); F_{ij}: T = kg·A⁻¹·s⁻² (magnetic field)
conservationLaws: ∂_{[μ}F_{νρ]} = 0 — Bianchi identity / homogeneous Maxwell equations (Gauss-B + Faraday)
∂_μJ^μ = 0 — charge conservation (follows from ∂_μ∂_νF^{μν} = 0 by antisymmetry of F)
∂_νT^{μν} = F^{μν}J_ν — energy-momentum not conserved for field alone; Lorentz force density is the source term
constraints: Gauge redundancy: A_μ → A_μ + ∂_μλ(x) leaves F_{μν} strictly invariant — F is physical, A carries gauge freedom
Bianchi identity ∂_{[μ}F_{νρ]} = 0 is automatic when F = dA (closedness of the 2-form)
Reality condition: all components of F_{μν} are real in classical EM
observables: Electric field: E^i = cF^{0i} — directly measurable via force on test charge at rest
Magnetic field: B^i = −(1/2)ε^{ijk}F_{jk} — measurable via force on moving charge
Lorentz 4-force on charge q: f^μ = qF^μ_ν u^ν (covariant form of F = q(E + v×B))
I₁ = 2(B² − E²/c²): tells you whether the field is 'more magnetic' or 'more electric' in a Lorentz-invariant sense
• I₁ > 0: there EXISTS a Lorentz frame in which E⃗ = 0 (purely magnetic in that frame)
• I₁ < 0: there EXISTS a Lorentz frame in which B⃗ = 0 (purely electric in that frame)
• I₁ = 0 with I₂ = 0: null field — electromagnetic radiation (plane waves); E = cB and E⃗⊥B⃗ in every frame
• I₁ = 0 with I₂ ≠ 0: no standard frame simplification available
I₂ ∝ E⃗·B⃗: measures 'helicity' — whether E and B have a common projection axis
• I₂ = 0: E⃗ ⊥ B⃗ in every inertial frame (e.g., all radiation, static pure-E or pure-B fields)
• I₂ ≠ 0: E⃗ and B⃗ retain a nonzero dot product in EVERY frame — absolute geometric fact
• I₂ is a CP-odd observable: it changes sign under parity (E → E, B → −B) or time reversal
Stress-energy tensor: T^{μν} = F^{μα}F^ν_α − (1/4)η^{μν}F_{αβ}F^{αβ} — directly involves I₁ in the trace term

fields: J^μ = (cρ, J⃗) — 4-current density (source of the field)
*F_{μν} = (1/2)ε_{μνρσ}F^{ρσ} — Hodge dual tensor; swaps E⃗ ↔ cB⃗
interactions: Minimal coupling to charged matter: ∂_μ → D_μ = ∂_μ + iqA_μ/ℏ
Electromagnetic duality: (E⃗, B⃗) → (cB⃗, −E⃗/c) maps F → *F, leaving Maxwell vacuum equations invariant
gaugeSymmetries: Local U(1): A_μ → A_μ + ∂_μλ(x); F_{μν} is invariant — gauge freedom in potential
Poincaré (Lorentz boosts + rotations): F_{μν} transforms as a covariant 2-tensor; I₁ and I₂ are preserved
Electromagnetic duality (vacuum only): (F, *F) → (*F, −F) maps solutions to solutions
Noether's theorem: U(1) gauge invariance → ∂_μJ^μ = 0 (charge conservation)

dependencies: Minkowski metric η_{μν} = diag(+1,−1,−1,−1) for raising/lowering indices
Maxwell's equations in covariant form (source and Bianchi)
Exterior algebra: F = dA is an exact 2-form; dF = 0 follows automatically
Cayley-Hamilton theorem (completeness of invariants for antisymmetric tensors in 4D)
assumptions: Flat Minkowski spacetime — no gravitational curvature, R_{μνρσ} = 0
SI units with explicit factors of c; results hold in natural units by setting c = 1
Classical field theory — no quantum corrections or path integrals
No magnetic monopoles (Bianchi identity ∂_{[μ}F_{νρ]} = 0 holds globally, not just locally)
